subject: DeepWell demo: intermittent live chunk silence during high-throughput demo (urgent)
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia@deepwell.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Live demo interruption — streaming output went silent 

Mina,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. During the live Q&A our downstream UI stopped receiving chunks for roughly 18–22 seconds on three requests; the session then recovered without a full disconnect. We captured the client-side timestamps and a server request-id (rq-7c9b2f). Attached are session_logs_0904.txt and a small packet capture (trace_pcap_0904.zip).

Impact we saw:
- Two demo requests stalled in the middle of generation (partial tokens shown, then silence).
- Overall stream throughput dropped ~60% during the incident window.
- Several WebSocket clients showed a 1006 code at the client library level but reconnected automatically and resumed.

This was our final demo for procurement execs — they asked for an explanation and whether this is likely under our expected traffic. Can you advise root cause and a short-term mitigation?

Amelia Torres
Head of Integrations, DeepWell AI
amelia@deepwell.ai
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: session_logs_0904.txt (text), trace_pcap_0904.zip (pcap)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@deepwell.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live demo interruption — streaming output went silent

Amelia — sorry you hit that during the demo, and thank you for the artifacts. I’m escalating to SRE immediately (cc'd) to triage logs and traces. Top-level: we are treating this as P1 because it affects streamed token delivery and could be visible to other customers under burst load.

Initial ask from us:
- David, please correlate rq-7c9b2f across edge logs + backend traces and check for chunked-transfer / keepalive anomalies.
- Amelia, can you confirm whether you were connected to our hosted endpoint via WebSocket or using chunked HTTP streaming for the demo? That helps narrow the proxy path.

Short-term mitigation we will pursue as we triage:
- Enable streaming-fallback route to a lower-latency replica for affected sessions for the next hour.
- Temporarily increase edge pool capacity for the us-west region.
- If chunked frames are freezing inside the proxy, we may need an immediate proxy config tweak (reduce buffer timeout / disable HTTP buffering for that route).

I’ll update you within 90 minutes with findings.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Amelia Torres <amelia@deepwell.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live demo interruption — streaming output went silent

Mina / Amelia — quick technical notes from initial triage (log snippets attached inline). I correlated rq-7c9b2f and found the following pattern:

1) Edge -> proxy: the client established a WebSocket upgrade but some demo clients used chunked HTTP streaming (Transfer-Encoding: chunked). Both entry paths converge to the same streaming worker pool.

2) At ~08:12:34 the worker processing rq-7c9b2f sent several chunk frames, then no further chunks were emitted for ~20s. The worker PID shows it still had an active inference session and was responsive to health pings; however, Envoy (our proxy) reported connection-level upstream resets and subsequently retransmitted the session to another worker which resumed output.

3) Metrics during the window (us-west edge): 99th percentile token latency jumped from ~240ms to ~1.8s; 5xx rate increased from 0.2% to 1.8% for the route; throughput per worker fell by ~58%.

4) There are a cluster of events where Envoy's HTTP/1.1 buffer hit the configured max (default_input_buffer), and at threshold it paused forwarding chunked frames until upstream yielded more bytes. In addition, keepalive probes from the worker to the GPU backend were intermittently timing out (TCP retransmits).

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a combination of transient backend latency (GPU scheduling jitter during a short burst) and proxy buffering/backpressure causing chunked-transfer frames to be stalled rather than streamed.

Immediate actions I recommend (we can run any with Mina's sign-off):
- Flip the route to streaming-fallback to bypass HTTP buffering (already prepared).
- Apply a short-lived proxy config change: increase max buffer bytes and lower buffer timeout so smaller chunks pass through fast.
- Pin affected worker to a different GPU host to rule out node-level overload.

I’m collecting full traces and will post to the incident doc.

— David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Vanessa / Soojin / Rishi — FYI and request for exec-level visibility. DeepWell (DW-3921, procurement running this week) saw streaming chunk silence during a live exec demo. David's early triage points to proxy buffering + transient backend jitter.

Customer ask / business impact:
- Procurement execs are concerned this will surface in production traffic; this demo had senior buyers in the call.
- We should consider a short-term goodwill gesture (recommended: one-month hosted credit) if DeepWell escalates procurement consequences.

Technical plan we've started:
- Streaming-fallback route enabled for their project.
- Proxy buffer tweak + scale-up of edge pool in us-west (in progress).
- Trace and pcap uploaded to incident doc: https://drive.redwood/company/DeepWell/incident-0904-notes.md

Asks:
- Vanessa, please prep a customer note that acknowledges the issue, summarizes mitigations, and offers the goodwill gesture if procurement pushes. Keep tone empathetic; avoid technical deep-dive unless they request it.
- Rishi / Soojin, please advise if we need to brief CEO/COO for an account-level escalation (this is a net-new enterprise opportunity — procurement may delay).

I’ll update with root cause and recommended permanent fix by EOD.

— Mina
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 06 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: DeepWell demo incident — exec awareness & customer response

Team — follow-up from the hotfix window:

What we did:
- Rolled the streaming-fallback route for DeepWell projects and reduced HTTP/1.1 input buffer to 64k for the route (was 256k).
- Redeployed a targeted worker group pinned to lower-util GPU hosts for their sessions for the next 48 hours.
- Turned on more aggressive backend keepalive retries to reduce transient TCP stalls.

Observed outcome (post-change):
- No further silent-chunk windows in the 24h observation window; token latency 99th percentile returned to ~260ms.
- 5xx rate for the route normalized to 0.25% in us-west.

Next steps (permanent fixes):
- Runtime: add detection to detect chunk-frame stalls and auto-failover session to hot-path within 5s. (owner: Markus)
- Proxy: revisit default buffer and timeout settings for heavy streaming routes; consider per-customer overrides. (owner: David)
- Customer comms: Vanessa to send customer note; include apology, summary of actions, and offer of one-month credit pending procurement outcome.

If leadership wants a short exec readout, I can prepare a 1-page brief and include timeline, root cause evidence, and remediation plan. Recommend we avoid an immediate public postmortem until we've validated the runtime detection change.

— Markus
